title: Circles
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.geo.circles.circumference: Circumference = π × diameter = 2 × π × radius. Write the number in front of π.
hints.geo.circles.area: Area = π × radius × radius. If you're given the diameter, halve it first.
hints.geo.circles: Around: πd. Inside: πr². Radius is half the diameter.

misconceptionMessages.geo.circle-diameter-radius: Check radius vs. diameter: the radius goes from the center to the edge; the diameter goes all the way across (twice the radius).
misconceptionMessages.geo.circle-area-circumference: Two formulas: around the circle (circumference) is 2πr; inside (area) is πr².
misconceptionMessages.geo.half-forgot: It's a half circle: take half of the whole circle's area.

sections.title: Circumference
sections.objective: Find the distance around a circle, in terms of π.
explain: Every circle's circumference is a little more than 3 times its diameter: exactly π times.
We write answers like 10π, without multiplying out π.

steps: The radius is 5 cm, so the diameter is 10 cm.

sections.title: Area of a circle
sections.objective: Find the area of a circle, in terms of π.
explain: The area formula uses the radius squared: radius times radius.

steps: The diameter is 8 m, so the radius is 4 m.
So A = 16π m² (not 64π: that would use the diameter).

sections.key: Area = π × radius². Halve the diameter first if that's what you're given.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: Around the edge: 2πr. Inside: πr². Radius = half the diameter.
